## Proof

**Claim:** Yes. Every $\mathbb{R}$-algebra homomorphism $h: \mathbb{R}[V] \to \mathbb{R}$ is of the form $ev_x$ for some $x \in V$.

**Setup.** Let $V \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be an affine real algebraic set with coordinate ring
$$\mathbb{R}[V] = \mathbb{R}[x_1, \dots, x_n] / I(V),$$
where $I(V) = \{f \in \mathbb{R}[x_1,\dots,x_n] : f|_V = 0\}$ is the vanishing ideal of $V$. Let $\pi: \mathbb{R}[x_1,\dots,x_n] \to \mathbb{R}[V]$ be the quotient map.

**Step 1: Lift $h$ to the polynomial ring.** Given an $\mathbb{R}$-algebra homomorphism $h: \mathbb{R}[V] \to \mathbb{R}$, the composition
$$\varphi := h \circ \pi : \mathbb{R}[x_1,\dots,x_n] \to \mathbb{R}$$
is an $\mathbb{R}$-algebra homomorphism.

**Step 2: $\varphi$ is evaluation at a real point.** The polynomial ring $\mathbb{R}[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ is the free commutative $\mathbb{R}$-algebra on the $n$ generators $x_1,\dots,x_n$. Therefore $\varphi$ is completely determined by the values $a_i := \varphi(x_i) \in \mathbb{R}$, $i = 1,\dots,n$. Setting $x = (a_1,\dots,a_n) \in \mathbb{R}^n$, we have
$$\varphi(f) = f(x) = ev_x(f) \quad \text{for all } f \in \mathbb{R}[x_1,\dots,x_n].$$
This step uses only that $\mathbb{R}$ is the base ring and that the polynomial ring is free on its generators — **no algebraic closure is required**.

**Step 3: The point $x$ lies in $V$.** Since $\varphi = h \circ \pi$ and $\ker \pi = I(V)$, the map $\varphi$ vanishes on $I(V)$:
$$f(x) = \varphi(f) = 0 \quad \text{for all } f \in I(V).$$
Thus $x \in V(I(V)) := \{p \in \mathbb{R}^n : f(p) = 0 \text{ for all } f \in I(V)\}$.

Now we use the Galois connection between algebraic sets and ideals. Since $V$ is an algebraic set, $V = V(J)$ for some ideal $J$. By definition $I(V) \supseteq J$, so $V(I(V)) \subseteq V(J) = V$. Conversely, every $f \in I(V)$ vanishes on $V$ by definition, so $V \subseteq V(I(V))$. Hence
$$V(I(V)) = V.$$
Therefore $x \in V$.

**Step 4: $h = ev_x$ on $\mathbb{R}[V]$.** For any $\bar{f} \in \mathbb{R}[V]$ (where $\bar{f} = \pi(f)$ for some polynomial $f$),
$$h(\bar{f}) = h(\pi(f)) = \varphi(f) = f(x) = ev_x(\bar{f}).$$
So $h = ev_x$ with $x \in V$. $\blacksquare$

**Remark.** The argument relies on two facts: (i) $\mathbb{R}$-algebra homomorphisms out of the polynomial ring are evaluations at real points (freeness of the polynomial ring), and (ii) $V(I(V)) = V$ for an algebraic set $V$ (the Galois connection / real Nullstellensatz at the level of algebraic sets). Neither requires $\mathbb{R}$ to be algebraically closed, in contrast to the general Hilbert Nullstellensatz over algebraically closed fields. The real subtlety over $\mathbb{R}$ — that $I(V(J))$ may be strictly larger than $J$ (the real radical) — does not affect this result, because we work with $I(V)$ (already a real ideal) rather than an arbitrary defining ideal $J$.
